extracted.intended_audience: investment advisers, exempt reporting advisers, and their legal/compliance counsel (entities subject to the Investment Advisers Act of 1940)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules and standards in 17 CFR Part 275 governing registration, filings, procedures, definitions, and compliance obligations for investment advisers under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. Used to determine how advisers must file, maintain records, avoid prohibited conduct, and satisfy definitional tests (e.g., family offices, foreign private advisers).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.0-2 General procedures for serving non-residents.
rubrics_metrics.description: General procedures for serving process, pleadings, or other papers on non-resident investment advisers, general partners and managing agents by serving any or all of its appointed agents under Forms ADV and ADV-NR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If serving a non-resident adviser or non-resident general partner/managing agent, furnish the Commission one copy for each named party and one additional copy for Commission records; the Secretary will promptly forward a copy to each named party by registered or certified mail at the party's last address filed with the Commission; the Secretary's certification that the Commission was served and forwarded the documents constitutes evidence of service. Definitions provided for 'managing agent', 'non-resident', and 'principal office and place of business' (see § 275.203A-3(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.0-3 References to rules and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of the term 'rules and regulations' for purposes of the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term refers to all rules and regulations adopted by the Commission pursuant to the Act, including the forms for registration and reports and the accompanying instructions thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.0-4 General requirements of papers and applications.
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and procedures governing filings, formal specifications, authorization, verification, statements of grounds, identification, and numbering of applications and other papers filed with the Commission under the Act (excluding registration applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings: papers must be delivered to the Secretary (deemed filed when actually received); filings made electronically with the IARD are deemed filed upon acceptance by IARD; special timing rules for IARD closures and annual December shutdown (timely if filed by next business day or by Jan 7 for Dec shutdown). Formal specifications: applications without prescribed form must be filed electronically under Regulation S-T; paper filings (including hardship exemptions) must be filed in quintuplicate; one copy signed by applicant; paper size generally 8½x11 (larger allowed if reduction makes illegible); left margin at least 1½ inches; binding left; black type for photocopying. Authorization: corporate/partnership applications must include concise statement of provisions authorizing signer and statement that signer is authorized; attach resolutions or quote pertinent provisions as exhibit if authorization depends on resolutions. Amendments must contain similar authorization statements or reference original. Agent/attorney signatures require power of attorney. Verification: every application/amendment/statement of fact must be verified by the person executing it; example verification form language provided. Statement of grounds: each application should briefly state reasons and cite Act provisions/rules relied upon. Name and address: every application must contain name and address of each applicant and point of contact. Definition: 'application' as used excludes applications for registration as an investment adviser. Numbering: manually signed originals (or duplicate originals) must be sequentially numbered and total number of pages set forth on first page; exhibit pages included.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.0-5 Procedure with respect to applications and other matters.
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps the Commission follows for proceedings initiated by filing an application or on the Commission's own motion, including notice, opportunity to request hearings, and issuance of orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of initiation published in the Federal Register will indicate earliest date an order may be entered and provide that interested persons may submit facts bearing on desirability of a hearing and request a hearing stating reasons and interest. An order will issue after the notice period unless Commission orders a hearing. The Commission will order a hearing if necessary or appropriate in the public interest or for investor protection, either upon request of any interested person or on its own motion. 'Application' defined as in § 275.0-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.0-6 Incorporation by reference in applications.
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on incorporating previously filed documents or parts thereof by reference as exhibits to applications filed with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any document or part filed with the Commission may be incorporated by reference as an exhibit to any application. If modifications occurred in the text since filing, registrant must file a statement containing the text of the modification and the date. Include an express statement clearly describing the specific location of the information being incorporated by reference; identify the original document and location within it; the statement must be made at the place where the information is required if applicable. Information must not be incorporated where such incorporation would render disclosure incomplete, unclear, or confusing — for example, do not incorporate from a second document if that second document itself incorporates relevant information by reference to a third document (unless permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.0-7 Small entities under the Investment Advisers Act for purposes of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'small business' or 'small organization' for purposes of Commission rulemaking under the Regulatory Flexibility Act as applied to investment advisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An investment adviser is a 'small business' or 'small organization' if it: (1) has assets under management of less than $25 million (or higher amount set by Commission), (2) did not have total assets of $5 million or more on the last day of most recent fiscal year, and (3) does not control, is not controlled by, and is not under common control with another adviser with assets under management of $25 million or more (or with any person, other than a natural person, that had total assets of $5 million or more). 'Control' and 'total assets' are defined with presumptions for corporations, partnerships, LLCs, and trusts.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.202(a)(1)-1 Certain transactions not deemed assignments.
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule that transactions which do not change actual control or management of an investment adviser are not assignments for purposes of section 205(a)(2) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise statement: a transaction that does not change actual control or management is not an assignment under section 205(a)(2). (Citations to Federal Register amendments provided.)

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.202(a)(11)(G)-1 Family offices.
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion and definitional rules specifying when a family office is not an 'investment adviser' for purposes of the Act, plus grandfathering and detailed definitions (family client, family member, key employee, control, affiliated family office, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A family office that: (1) has no clients other than family clients (with limited transitional treatment for certain non-family clients resulting from involuntary transfer), (2) is wholly owned by family clients and exclusively controlled by family members/family entities, and (3) does not hold itself out to the public as an investment adviser, is not considered an investment adviser. Grandfathering: persons meeting certain pre-1/1/2010 conditions may be excluded despite advising certain non-family persons. Extensive definitions clarify affiliated family office, control, executive officer, family client (enumerating family member, former family member, key employee, non-profit org funded exclusively by family clients, estates, trusts, irrevocable/revocable trusts, and companies wholly owned by family clients), family entity, family member (lineal descendants up to 10 generations plus spouses/spousal equivalents), former family member, key employee (participation in investment activities for at least 12 months, excluding pure clerical staff), spousal equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.202(a)(30)-1 Foreign private advisers.
rubrics_metrics.description: Safe-harbor rules and definition for determining clients and applicability of section 202(a)(30) of the Act for foreign private advisers, including who may be treated as a single client, special counting rules, definitions (assets under management, investor, in the United States, place of business, spousal equivalent), and holding out limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may deem certain natural persons (plus minor children, certain relatives sharing principal residence, accounts/trusts where they are only primary beneficiaries) to be a single client; a legal organization to which advice is given based on the organization's investment objectives (not individual owners) and two or more legal organizations with identical owners may be a single client. Special rules require counting an owner as a client in certain circumstances; do not count a private fund as a client if you count certain investors as US investors; a limited partnership/LLC is a client of any general partner/managing member. Definitions: 'assets under management' as per Form ADV Item 5.F; 'investor' specifics; 'in the United States' guidance (including exceptions for persons not in US at time they became client); 'place of business' and 'spousal equivalent' cross-references. Holding out: relying on this section does not mean you are holding yourself out generally to the US public solely because you participate in a non-public offering in the US of securities issued by a private fund under the Securities Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.203-1 Application for investment adviser registration.
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for applying for registration with the Commission as an investment adviser, including completing and filing Form ADV (Part 1A, Part 2A brochures, Part 3 Form CRS) electronically with the IARD, and transitional requirements for Form CRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To apply for registration, you must complete Form ADV by following its instructions and file Part 1A, the firm brochure(s) required by Part 2A, and Form CRS required by Part 3 electronically with the IARD unless you have a hardship exemption under § 275.203-3. Brochure supplements (Part 2B) are not required to be filed with the Commission. If you are not required to deliver a brochure or Form CRS to clients, you are not required to prepare or file them with the Commission. On/after June 30, 2020, the Commission will not accept any initial application that does not include a Form CRS satisfying Part 3; transitional filing deadlines noted. Each Form ADV considered filed upon IARD acceptance. Filing fees payable to FINRA (IARD operator).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.206(4)-5 (Political contributions — prohibitions and exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on providing investment advisory services to a government entity within two years after certain political contributions by the adviser or its covered associates, restrictions on payments to persons to solicit government entities, and coordination/solicitation restrictions; plus exceptions (de minimis, new covered associates, returned contributions) and exemptions by Commission upon application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is unlawful for registered (or certain exempt) advisers to provide compensated advisory services to a government entity within two years after a contribution to an official of the government entity by the adviser or a covered associate. Advisers (and covered associates) may not pay persons to solicit government entities unless the person is a regulated person or an officer/general partner/managing member/employee of the adviser, and may not coordinate or solicit others to make contributions/payments to an official or to a political party in the relevant jurisdiction. Exceptions include de minimis contributions by covered associates ($350 per election to officials entitled to vote for, $150 per election to others), limited exception for contributions made by individuals prior to becoming covered associates (if >6 months prior and they do not thereafter solicit clients), and limited returned-contribution remedy if discovered within 4 months, returned within 60 days, subject to limits on number of exceptions per year based on employee count and per-contributor limits. Prohibitions applied to covered investment pools; indirect acts that would produce violations if done directly are also prohibited. Commission may grant exemptions considering public interest, adviser policies, timing/amount/nature of contribution, and contributor's intent. Extensive definitions provided for contribution, covered associate, covered investment pool, executive officer, government entity, official, payment, plan or program of a government entity, regulated person, and solicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.206(4)-6 Proxy voting.
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements governing proxy voting for SEC-registered advisers: adopt and implement written policies and procedures, disclose how clients can obtain voting information, and describe proxy voting policies and furnish them upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registered or required to be registered under section 203, it is a fraudulent, deceptive, or manipulative act within section 206(4) to exercise voting authority with respect to client securities unless: (a) you adopt and implement written policies and procedures reasonably designed to ensure voting in clients' best interests, including how to address material conflicts between adviser and client; (b) you disclose to clients how they may obtain information about how you voted their securities; and (c) you describe your proxy voting policies and procedures to clients and, upon request, furnish a copy to the requesting client.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.206(4)-7 Compliance procedures and practices.
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory compliance policies, annual review, and chief compliance officer designation for registered or required-to-be-registered investment advisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered or required advisers must: (a) adopt and implement written policies and procedures reasonably designed to prevent violations of the Act and Commission rules by the adviser and supervised persons; (b) review at least annually the adequacy of such policies/procedures and the effectiveness of their implementation; and (c) designate an individual (a supervised person) responsible for administering the policies and procedures (Chief Compliance Officer).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.206(4)-8 Pooled investment vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition against making untrue statements or omitting material facts and against other fraudulent, deceptive, or manipulative acts with respect to investors or prospective investors in pooled investment vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is fraudulent, deceptive, or manipulative for an adviser to a pooled investment vehicle to: (1) make any untrue statement of material fact or omit a material fact so statements are misleading to any investor or prospective investor in the pooled vehicle; or (2) otherwise engage in any fraudulent, deceptive, or manipulative act, practice, or course of business with respect to any investor or prospective investor in the pooled vehicle. 'Pooled investment vehicle' is defined to include investment companies under section 3(a) of the Investment Company Act or companies that would be investment companies but for exclusions under sections 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.222-1 Definitions — Place of business and principal office.
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of 'place of business' and 'principal office and place of business' for purposes of section 222 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Place of business' means an office where the adviser regularly provides advisory services, solicits, meets with, or otherwise communicates with clients, and any other location held out to the public as a location where such services/communications are provided. 'Principal office and place of business' means the executive office from which officers/partners/managers direct, control, and coordinate the adviser's activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 275.222-2 Definition of 'client' for purposes of the national de minimis standard.
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule allowing advisers to rely on the 'client' definition in § 275.202(a)(30)-1 for purposes of section 222(d)(2) (national de minimis standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of section 222(d)(2), an investment adviser may rely upon the definition of 'client' provided by § 275.202(a)(30)-1 without giving regard to paragraph (b)(4) of that section.
